content:
**Formula 1 Grand Prix events that have taken place in Asia or the Middle‑East (up to and including the 2025 season) – and the driver who has won the most races at each circuit**

| # | Circuit (Country) | Grand Prix name (official title) | Years the race was held* | Driver with the most wins at that circuit | # of wins | Notes |
|---|-------------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------|----------|-------|
| 1 | **Bahrain International Circuit** – Bahrain | **Bahrain Grand Prix** (usually “Bahrain GP”) | 2004‑2025 (no race in 2011) | **Lewis Hamilton** | **6** (2008, 2011, 2014, 2015, 2021, 2022) |
| 2 | **Jeddah Corniche Circuit** – Saudi Arabia | **Saudi Arabian Grand Prix** | 2021‑2025 | **Max Verstappen** | **3** (2022, 2023, 2024). Hamilton won the inaugural 2021 race (1 win). |
| 3 | **Yas Marina Circuit** – Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates | **Abu Dhabi Grand Prix** | 2009‑2025 | **Lewis Hamilton** | **8** (2009, 2012, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2018, 2019, 2020) |
| 4 | **Marina Bay Street Circuit** – Singapore | **Singapore Grand Prix** | 2008, 2010‑2019, 2022‑2025 (2020‑21 cancelled) | **Tie – Lewis Hamilton & Sebastian Vettel** | **3 each**. Hamilton (2008, 2015, 2022). Vettel (2011, 2012, 2013). |
| 5 | **Shanghai International Circuit** – China | **Chinese Grand Prix** | 2004‑2008, 2014‑2019, 2024‑2025 (2020‑23 cancelled) | **Lewis Hamilton** | **5** (2008, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2019). |
| 6 | **Suzuka International Racing Course** – Japan | **Japanese Grand Prix** (held at Suzuka except 2007) | 1987‑2006, 2009‑2025 (except 2020‑21 cancelled) | **Lewis Hamilton** | **6** (2007, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2020). |
| 7 | **Fuji Speedway** – Japan | **Japanese Grand Prix** (only 2007) | 2007 only | **Felipe Massa** | **1** (the sole 2007 race). |
| 8 | **Sepang International Circuit** – Malaysia | **Malaysian Grand Prix** | 1999‑2017 (no race 2009‑10, 2015‑16 cancelled) | **Sebastian Vettel** | **5** (2010‑2013, 2017). |
| 9 | **Buddh International Circuit** – India | **Indian Grand Prix** | 2011‑2013 | **Sebastian Vettel** | **3** (won all three editions). |
|10| **Baku City Circuit** – Azerbaijan (geographically in the Asian part of the Caucasus) | **Azerbaijan Grand Prix** | 2016‑2025 | **Tie – Lewis Hamilton & Max Verstappen** | **2 each**. Hamilton (2016, 2021). Verstappen (2022, 2023). |
|11| **Khalifa International Circuit** – Qatar* (future) | **Qatar Grand Prix** – *not yet held (first race scheduled for 2026). | – | – | – | Not included in the table because no race has taken place as of 2025. |

\* **Years the race was held** indicates the calendar years in which the Grand Prix actually took place. Some seasons were cancelled or postponed (e.g., COVID‑19 related cancellations in 2020‑2021 for Singapore and China).

---

### How the “most‑wins” driver was determined
* All race results from the inaugural event at each circuit up to the end of the 2025 season were considered.  
* If two or more drivers share the highest win‑total, the entry is marked as a **tie** (as shown for Singapore and Baku).  
* For circuits that hosted a Grand Prix only once (e.g., Fuji), the sole winner naturally holds the “most wins” record with a single victory.

---

### Quick take‑aways
* **Lewis Hamilton** dominates the Middle‑East (Bahrain, Abu Dhabi) and also leads at key Asian venues (Suzuka, Shanghai, Singapore – tied).  
* **Sebastian Vettel** is the most successful driver on the newer Asian street/modern circuits (Sepang, India, Singapore – tied).  
* **Max Verstappen** has already eclipsed Hamilton at the Saudi Arabian GP and shares the lead at Baku after just a few seasons.  

Feel free to ask for deeper stats (e.g., podium counts, pole positions) or for any updates once the 2026 season begins!

### How the “most‑wins” driver was determined
* All race results from the inaugural event at each circuit up to the end of the 2025 season were considered.  
* If two or more drivers share the highest win‑total, the entry is marked as a **tie** (as shown for Singapore and Baku).  
* For circuits that hosted a Grand Prix only once (e.g., Fuji), the sole winner naturally holds the “most wins” record with a single victory.

---

### Quick take‑aways
* **Lewis Hamilton** dominates the Middle‑East (Bahrain, Abu Dhabi) and also leads at key Asian venues (Suzuka, Shanghai, Singapore – tied).  
* **Sebastian Vettel** is the most successful driver on the newer Asian street/modern circuits (Sepang, India, Singapore – tied).  
* **Max Verstappen** has already eclipsed Hamilton at the Saudi Arabian GP and shares the lead at Baku after just a few seasons.
